title: Add a newcomer introduction and glossary to the explainer page
summary: The explainer page (rendered by xtask/src/site.rs from studies/firstmate-work-handling) jumps straight into states, counters and transitions without saying what firstmate is. I read this as adding a plain-language "start here" section: what firstmate is, how a piece of work moves through it, and a glossary of terms. Every sentence in it must cite claims, as the page's existing rule requires.

defaults_applied.how: The page is for outside readers, which is the point of the request.
Every new sentence cites a claim, or is plainly about the page's own structure.
New rendering code gets tests; cargo test and clippy must pass.
One focused change to the page renderer.
I took the missing context from the xtask renderer and the study files, not from a question.
The verifier runs the site build and the tests.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: 'Never seen firstmate' means the page lacks context and definitions, not that its facts are wrong.
The page stays generated from the study JSON by xtask; no hand-edited HTML.
The page stays a single self-contained HTML file with no scripts or external links, as the existing tests require.
Existing claims are enough to ground the intro; no new study claims are needed.
Neither the workflow file nor any governance file changes.

acceptance_criteria.text: The rendered page opens with a section before 'States of a piece of work' that says in plain words what firstmate is (a supervisor that ships with a crew) and gives a short walk-through of one piece of work from start to finish.
A glossary defines each term the page uses without explanation (for example state, counter, transition, trigger, guard, claim, pin), in wording a reader new to firstmate can follow.
Each factual sentence in the new section cites a claim id from claims.json. Any fixed explanatory text describes only the page's own structure and makes no claim about firstmate.
Run `cargo test -p xtask`: all tests pass, including a new test that the page contains the intro and glossary, and that the existing citation checks still reject an uncited element.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`: both are clean.
Run `cargo run -p xtask -- site` from the repository root: it succeeds and writes the page without errors.

out_of_scope: Re-studying firstmate or changing the study's claims, model or findings
Restyling or redesigning the page layout
Changing the Pages workflow or deployment
